I just want to say that you should be wary and careful of deep discount from Hitman World of Assassination. As of today 11/28/2024, there is a 90% discount for Hitman World of Assassination PART ONE which is the same map/campaign as Hitman 1. 

The little rebranding of Hitman 3 to Hitman World of Assassination and then include Hitman (1) and Hitman 2 in it as if they're new content is sneaky at best and dishonest at worst. Check out World of Assassination Upgrade Pack and you'll find that it will only add 6 more new maps: Berlin, Carpathian Mountains, Chongqing, Dartmoor, Dubai, Mendoza. Everything else is Hitman 1 and Hitman 2 maps.

I already owned Hitman 1 and Hitman 2, I shouldn't have to look up Reddit guide on how to BUY a fucking game and what it includes. If you are confused like I was, please check this out: https://www.reddit.com/r/HiTMAN/comments/18w8zet/2024_guide_to_buying_hitman_3_and_world_of/

Buying guide: cheapest way to unlock full game with all maps.

1. Wait for sale. 
2. Buy HITMAN World of Assassination for €27,99
3. Buy HITMAN 3 Access Pass: HITMAN 2 Expansion for €6,99, this gives you access to Haven Island, New York and the Sniper Maps.

You can skip the rest, the deluxe edition is not really worth your money unless you've finished the game and want something new. Some of the celebrity dlc's are fun, but overpriced, only buy on sale.

For those having trouble buying the game or getting confused by it, [u] get the NORMAL VERSION + HITMAN 3 Access Pass: HITMAN 2 Expansion[/u] for all the main content/maps, avoiding paying more for any braindead cosmetics. Goodluck and keep hitting men.

How to buy the game (Yes I kid you not you need help with this)

[b]Standard Edition:[/b] For those who just want to play Hitman 3 and those who already own 1 and 2

[b]Deluxe Edition: [/b] Same as standard but with the 'Deluxe Pack' at a £5 discount compared to if you bought it separately (Apparently the deluxe pack is not worth it according to my friend who bought it on Epic Games at a lower price)

[b]HITMAN Trilogy:[/b] If you DON'T own any of the Hitman games and want to play them all on one place, despite being the most expensive one this is not a complete package and does not include the 'Deluxe Pack'

[b]Seven Deadly Sins:[/b] All of the Year 1 DLC for the game (Apparently the price has been raised and discounted to make it seem like a better deal)

[b]Hitman 2 Gold Access Pass:[/b] Essentially the content from the Hitman 2 Gold edition but in Hitman 3, do not buy this if you already own Hitman 2. This is so overpriced as well, This does not include the game itself so if you want to play all of the 1 and 2 content get the Trilogy pack or buy the games separate and link your account to get them.

How to link your account if you own Hitman 1 or Hitman 2:
If you go to profile.hitman.com you can link your IOI account to transfer your progress AND LOCATIONS to Hitman 3 so you don't need to grind or re-purchase levels you already own. This isn't explained well enough before buying editions of the game.

I accidentally bought the wrong version (Trilogy) despite owning everything in 1 and 2 so had to refund the game and buy the standard edition. I don't want anyone else going through the pain of realising they bought the wrong edition and being unable to play for a few hours or so whilst their refund goes through.

If you don't care enough about steam you can play the trilogy on gamepass or buy it for cheap on epic games.

Hope this helps : ) If you could mark this as helpful that would be appreciated so other people don't get done over.

Be careful when buying!! The purchase options and DLC is very confusing and its easy to buy something you didn't want. The one you are probably looking for is "HITMAN World of Assassination". This is basically the modern hitman 1, 2, and 3 games packed into one big game.

"HITMAN World of Assassination Episode: Sapienza" only grants you access to one mission which i do not recommend at all. "HITMAN World of Assassination Part One" Gives you access to the entire hitman 1 campaign, but not 2 or 3.

The deluxe edition comes with a bunch of escalation missions, which are extremely short missions where you have to kill the target in a specific way with specific conditions. These just piggyback off of main story maps and don't add anything new so i do not recommend paying so much for these. It also comes with some extra cosmetics you probably won't care about, as well as two bonus story missions; the big meat of this pack. While these two missions are great, you don't need to buy the deluxe edition for them! You can buy these separately under the DLC "HITMAN 3 access pass: HITMAN 2 expansion". Of course, you can play through the game until you reach these missions before deciding if you want to buy it or not.

TLDR; "HITMAN World of Assassination" Is the option you will want to buy. The DLC "HITMAN 3 access pass: HITMAN 2 expansion" gives you access to two more story missions. If you don't know if you want the DLC, you can play through the game until you reach those missions to see if you would want it. If you wish to get all the achievements, you will need this DLC to do that, but nothing extra.

Lastly, get the game on sale! There is no need to pay 70 bucks for this game. You can frequently find this game on sale for less than half as much.

Complaint #1

I wanted to be able to recommend this, but the simple reality is the servers are so absolutely terrible that it constantly gets in the way of game play with disconnections.

I'd over looked the online element in the previous two games because the connections were relatively stable and despite being a single player game, the online elements were worth it; contracts mode is the heart of the endless replay value.

Complaint #2

It's wildly over priced for the small amount of content presented here.

I don't care that it was released to Epic first, I don't care that it's been on sale before being brought to Steam and then released on Steam at full price; what I care about is that this isn't $60 worth of game compared to the previous two in the trilogy. And the DLC on top of it brings that price to $120 while adding nothing noteworthy, not even real missions or locations.

EDIT: (years later) [i] Price comparisons removed.[/i] The previous two games are no longer available and the now renamed WOA (replacing Hitman 3) has had price changes. However, that just makes it even more convoluted for how to buy things and there's now a bunch of content new buyers can never get. And don't even ask me to try and explain the DLC situation or which ones are no longer available or why so many of them are wildly over priced for fractional amounts of content. This went from a great series to a drip feed cash grab over time.

Now realize, this is coming from a player who put 1000+ hours into each of the previous games, and the only reason I'll put another 1000+ into this one will be due to the fact you can play the other seasons inside of it.

Summary:

Beyond that, you don't need me to tell you the gameplay itself is good. You can play the demo yourself, it's free. If you've played the prior two games, this is more of the same, just less of it. There's fewer story missions per location, most of the locations are fairly small; even the ones that are technically large have a lot of open space with nothing in them. There's less challenges, less escalations, and the DLC (which you have to pay for) add only escalations that in prior games were free.

It basically comes down to this:

Hitman 3 is a glorified expansion pack to the trilogy that has the least content of the three seasons. Do you want it? Probably, but do yourself a favor and wait until it's on sale for a price you won't hate yourself for paying.

[strike]If you don't own any of the trilogy yet, pick up Hitman 2 Gold + GOTY Legacy Pack, even at $120 full price it's a huge volume of content compared to Hitman 3 for $120 which is a fraction of the size. And of course Hitman 2 Gold goes on sale several times a year for deep discounts so you won't even need to pay full price. And if and when you do get around to buying Hitman 3, your progress will carry over from 2.[/strike] EDIT: Well, they discontinued the previous games, renamed Hitman 3 into "World of Assassination" and this is now the only way to buy the trilogy if you didn't already own the previous games.

I'm still not going to change this to recommended, because they've also made it way too convoluted for how to buy everything. I used to write a guide for it, but it's so convoluted even I'm not keeping up with it. And the missing DLC would take another essay to explain…

This could have been one of the greatest games of all time, in fact, it should have been. And yet they somehow managed to abuse it and their fan base.

You can buy it, but don't expect me to recommend it.

Keep in mind that steam reviews only ask if you recommend the game or not. I've already stated it's a good game, I'm just not recommending it anyway due to the terrible marketing, abusive DLC, horrible support and myriad of other issues that plague the franchise and its new publishers. They took a great series and decided to just keep abusing the fan base instead of focusing on making the game better.
---

Bottom line: Hitman (season) 3 (now renamed World of Assassination) is functionally a good game, but the mess this company has become and the DLC nightmare is unforgivable. Buy at your own risk.

If you're planning to buy the complete experience, keep in mind that Hitman 3 Deluxe pack is different from World of Assassination Deluxe pack - The former contains deluxe content for Hitman 3, whereas the latter contains the H3 Deluxe pack, as well as Hitman 2 Expansion pack and the Seven Deadly Sins expansion.

As for additional packs, Trinity Pack, Street Art Pack and Makeshift Pack are all purely customization items, Sarajevo Six Campaign pack is a playable story DLC that adds extra targets to certain levels, and the other packs (The Undying Pack, The Disruptor Pack, The Drop Pack and some other packs that might appear later) are seasonal content - this is content that is free to play for a limited time. Buying these packs grants you extra customization items, as well as permanent access to the content after the seasonal period expires. In order to gain access to the content and the items, this can be purchased even after the season has ended.

Hitman is one of my favorite franchises and the new trilogy is a perfect successor to Silent Assassin, Contracts and Blood Money, but this pricing model is embarrassing. If Io Interactive wants to charge the price of a full new release (or four new releases) for a title that had come out a year ago on a different storefront, that's their prerogative. In the meantime, prospective customers still need to consult a flow chart to determine what they're getting with which purchase, deal with server issues for a single-player game that has no business requiring a continuous online connection and contend with a needlessly roundabout progression carryover process that could have easily been substituted by importing a local save file from Hitman 1/2. 

Io Interactive's game developers deserve props for delivering a dense, polished stealth sandbox. Regrettably, their publishing branch also deserves all the flak they get for extorting their fanbase like this. I recommend a purchase only on sale or after a price drop. Alternatively, play it on GamePass. 

EDIT: had to revise "complete" package price because I had overlooked that the Trilogy Premium Add-On Bundle also includes the Deluxe Edition of Hitman 3. Hitman 2 Gold Bundle and Hitman 1 GOTY Edition is advised for the people that missed only one of those two games. Apologies to anyone affected.

Great gameplay, like all of the games in the trilogy. And like all of the games in the trilogy, they've done their best to ruin it by tying 90% of the single-player, fully offline gameplay to being "online." If you can't get a connection to their flaky servers, you cannot make any progress in the game, unlock anything or meaningfully replay missions. If you're not in online mode, the game only has a few hours of rewarding content.

This is just being hostile to users. There's no need for it to work this way; all of the content for achievements and unlocks and progression is available offline. The only thing you *need* to be online for is to get new escalations. These let you replay the original missions in different ways that, frankly, I don't enjoy. I *do* enjoy the career progression and unlocking new starts and devices, and I should be able to do that without having an internet connection at that moment. When this game stops selling enough new copies to support the cost of running the servers, they'll take them down and this game will be permanently crippled because they've made so much of the offline game play needlessly require a connection to their servers.

Also, this game allegedly lets you play the content from the previous games you own, but it turns out that it only does so if you've participated in their data collection in the past. Does it check the steam store to see what you own? Nope. Does it check the progress recorded in the game files on your machine? Nope. The only way it will let you play the previous games' maps is if you've signed up for an IOI account. I never have. I will have to create an IOI account I do not want, re-install THREE HUNDRED FUCKING GIGS of previous games and start them up just so I can log into my unwanted IOI account, let it send them a bunch of information about my game progress that is none of their fucking business, and then hope that it actually unlocks the content in the current game.

The VR is nearly unplayable and way more trouble than it's worth. They're apparently too busy making new online escalation missions to fix the actual game.

Finally, fuck Epic store exclusivity. I get that Valve takes an unreasonably large cut from Steam sales. If IOI had sold this game direct or via itch.io, I would have bought it that way just to support them, but the Epic store is buggy, barely functional, anti-consumer trash even all these years after they launched it. Epic charges less because they add no value and their lousy software detracts from the player's experience.

If you're buying this to play the standard version of this game, then it is pretty good. Honestly, this trilogy of games is the best Hitman content there is. The open levels, the freedom it allows, the crazy game moments you get to create, it's all fantastic. But I bought this to play it in VR, and if you are looking to do the same, you should definitely wait.

As a VR game, this is the jankiest game I have ever played. I've played indie games developed by a single person that are leagues ahead of this. There is so much wrong with it, it is hard to even begin. When I first started the game, I had to go back to the desktop to tell it I wanted to play it in VR. Then I sat staring at the intro screen while it told me to press "enter"; a key I don't have in VR. I finally realized that the game was minimized and apparently didn't recognize the VR controls, so I went to the desktop again to fix that. Haven't even started the game yet, and I had to leave it twice just to get to the menu. Also, the menu screen was off-center so I was tilting my head up 45 degrees to even see it. I finally make it into the training mission so I can figure out how it all works in VR, and it just got jankier from there.

You cannot physically move from your starting spot, as the character model does not follow you. You cannot physically crouch, as the game will think you're just going out of bounds. If my hands are in my view when I try to sprint, everything jitters. I figured this all out before even moving ten feet from the starting position. I go along with the tutorial, and it wants me to strangle a worker unconscious and steal his clothes. I grab him as I'm instructed, and his torso contorts wildly and glitches all over the place. He collapses, then just floats away like a balloon. It was kind of hilarious, but I wasn't expecting to see new bugs like this introduced into the game. Anytime I try to choke someone unconscious or use the garrote wire, they turn into balloon people and float away. OK then, I figure I'll hit my next target with the crowbar to knock him out. Nope. For some reason, it takes five or more hits to the head with a crowbar to take someone down, all the while they call out for help, pull out a gun, and shoot me. Throwing the crowbar does work, once you can figure out the unintuitive throwing mechanics. Think you can just aim and throw an object like literally any other VR game? Of course not. Don't be ridiculous. So finally, I just resorted to punching, which is the only (mostly) reliable way of taking out quietly. But don't punch too fast, or the game won't track your hands and your fists go through the person. Too slow and you'll just annoy them. Once you get the speed just right, sometimes you'll knock them out with one hit, but most likely, you will be awkwardly punching the back of some dude's head until he collapses.

Shooting firearms isn't much better. With a two handed weapon like a rifle, your left hand does nothing, and it just snaps to the front of the weapon when your hand is next to it. It does not actually stabilize the gun. You do not manually reload the guns, you push the reload button and it plays an animation (that should be a crime in a VR game). The pistols work alright, but you can't use two hands with it, and there's a delay between when the trigger is fully pulled and when it shoots, which is really awkward. Sometimes, items like the rifles become impossible to use as once I pick it up, it becomes frozen in place and there's nothing I can do about it. Once that happens, I just have to drop the item and forget about it.

You only have one holster for all items, positioned directly in the middle of your chest. If you move around a little too much, it gets lost and you will need to recenter the camera to find it. Your left hand doesn't can't actually do anything. You can't pick up anything with it or interact with any object, it is only used for aiming throwables and punching.

Well this rant has gone on for awhile, but I've encountered all of this before even putting 4 hours in the game, and it cost me $100, and I already own it on another system. And even if you disregard all the jank, I cannot possible understand how they decided to packaged these games. Go scroll up to the buy options. Look at the ridiculous amount of ways IOI is selling this. Gold editions, premium editions, add on packs, DLC. If I need a flow chart to understand what it is you're selling, it's too goddamn complicated. And why the hell are the standard levels considered DLC? It's just the normal game. Why would anyone want to buy the levels individually? You have 3 games here IOI, just sell three games. It shouldn't be this complicated.

I know that was a lot of negative, but I do think they can fix a lot of these issues over time, and I genuinely love the Hitman trilogy. And even with just the standard edition, it is a LOT of content. I'm doing what I can to overcome the control hurdles, because the controls really do not translate well to VR. But I am having some fun with it. It's quite fun to screw with random NPC's in VR, and the amount of detail in each level is just amazing. Now that I'm seeing it in VR, I can really notice a lot more of the levels, and it is impressive. Long story short, if you're buying this to play it in VR, just don't. Save your money and wait until they fix these glaring issues, if they ever do. I'm going to keep it because I do have faith that the studio will fix it, but it is absurd that they released it like this.

The game design is largely identical to the previous two entries, so I will only list notable changes here.
[b]Objectively good changes[/b]
▲ Some of the contextual keybinds have been altered to remove contextual confusion. Most notably, hiding a body in a container uses a different button than stepping into a container to hide yourself.
▲ Item and outfit selection menus now remember your previous choices, so if you have a preferred standard loadout you don't need to manually pick it every time
[b]Subjectively good changes[/b]
►► Sound design is improved. The soundscape of the 4th mission is especially good. 
► Missions have more variety compared to the previous two games.
► NPCs' idle chatter dialogue has variants where they discuss different subjects. So, consecutively restarting a difficult mission does not end up sounding as repetitive.
► Keypads with codes to unlock doors have been added. Players can write down codes and voluntarily sequence-break levels if they want, but other players can employ some self-discipline and only use codes after discovering them from the source.
► Less reliance on unlocks via challenges. I understand that challenges are there to inspire players, but some players want to inspire themselves, and I think it's good that things are not locked behind challenges.
► The game's theme and atmosphere are darker than the previous two games
► Several missions have in-gameplay introduction sequences, but in consecutive playthroughs you can pick a starting location that was specifically positioned right after them, as a skip feature.
[b]Subjectively bad changes[/b] 
◄ The missions are easier overall than in the previous games. I don't think it was necessary to lower the challenge.
◄ Placement of useful tools is a bit too convenient. No need to think about where you can find a crowbar to drop something on a target, because it always seems to be right next to it.
◄ Permanently unlockable shortcuts through levels have been added, but they seem to be more of a tutorial feature to ensure that players become aware of those options. I'm not sure I agree with the idea of players permanently influencing the challenge of navigation through levels. You don't get to just go up a ladder before kicking it down first in Dark Souls and that's for a reason.
◄ The new "camera" item seems redundant. It's just a slower way of gaining intel and a pointless delay in activating objects that might still require keys for them anyway.
◄ Freelancer mode is gimmicky and unimmersive. Its rules are arbitrary and take you right out of the experience. The targets have insufficient justification for operating in locations that are very specifically related to the actual targets in the campaign. You are rewarded for specific assassination methods for no tactical or story reason. Intel on leaders is too weirdly specific, and most apparent characteristics are not utilized. The only good thing about Freelancer is that it doesn't overprioritize Silent Assassin rating.
◄◄ There doesn't appear to be any differences between difficulties when it comes to level design. The description of Master difficulty says that levels have additional enforcers and cameras, but I have not found any instances of this.
[b]Objectively bad changes[/b] 
▼▼▼ Server connectivity is actually worse than it was in previous games. You cannot have a play session of several hours without disconnecting at least once. And you know what that means. This singleplayer game is incapable of saving your progress locally without first phoning Denmark.
▼▼▼ If you are downloading something and thus have low bandwidth, [b]the game's loading times increase tenfold.[/b] The game attempts to contact the servers, and if the connection ultimately gets timed out due to low bandwidth, the game can crash.

Hitman isn't a game you just play through once. Each of more than 20 missions gives you a huge sandbox filled with different assassination opportunities, side stories, and challenges. You can easily spend tens of hours in every single map if you take your time to experiment and explore everything, and you will never stop discovering new things. And that's just the campaign. Additional game modes such as arcade contracts, user-created contracts, and the rogue-lite Freelancer mode put your skill, creativity and map knowledge to the test and give you pretty much infinite replayability. And it's moddable.

This being said, buying the game is apparently just as complex as the game itself, which is what most of the negative reviews are about. IOI still haven't figured out in nearly a decade how to market their game. People keep getting confused by the purchase options and buy the wrong version, and every purchase guide written by players is unnecessarily convoluted and makes the process even more confusing. So here's all you need to know:
- Free Starter Pack: You get the tutorial to see if you like the gameplay
- Part One: You get Hitman 1 plus DLC, and you can upgrade it to Standard in the in-game store
- Standard: You get Part One plus Hitman 2 and 3 without their DLC
- Deluxe: You get Standard plus the Hitman 2 and 3 DLC
- The additional DLC on the store page are not included in Deluxe, but they are not worth it
- There is no way to buy only Hitman 3. Hitman 1-3 don't exist as separate games anymore.

My personal recommendation: Play the Free Starter Pack a few times to explore all the possibilities in the two tutorial levels, watch the gameplay trailers on YouTube, and if you are intrigued, grab the Deluxe Edition on sale.

You know how gamers sometimes end up owning multiple copies of the same popular game across different platforms (looking at you, Skyrim and Fallout)? Well that’s exactly what happened to me with Hitman: World of Assassination. I have a physical copy of Hitman (2016) for PS4, deluxe physical edition digital of Hitman 2 for PS5 and now, as of writing this - Hitman WOA on Steam as well. Which brings me to my primary complaint with Hitman - the needly convoluted purchasing scheme that IO Interactive came up with for purchasing the game. I’m don’t think I’m exaggerating when I say you practically need a flowchart to understand it (there’s an entire Reddit infographic dedicated to explaining it - www.reddit.com/r/HiTMAN/comments/18w8zet/2024_guide_to_buying_hitman_3_and_world_of/). Short version: if you’re an achievement hunter aiming for 100%, get the Deluxe edition. With a confusing tiered pricing like that, SOMEONE COULD HURT THEMSELVES (in this case, that someone is me).

Despite the aforementioned issue, I have to admit that my 170+ hours with Hitman WOA were thoroughly enjoyable.  STRAIGHT SHOT: this is an exceptionally replayable game that puts a refreshing spin on the assassin genre with an emphasis on disguise changes and stealth. Every mission encourages experimentation and rewards curiosity and creativity if you take the time to figure out how to execute a kill in a specific manner. The variety in how you can eliminate targets is genuinely impressive as well. Whether you prefer carefully orchestrated ‘accidents’ (pushing someone off a roof while they’re watching a fireworks display) social stealth through disguises (serving sushi as a chef with a poisoned fugu), or bold, explosive takedowns (dropping an explosive gas canister down a chimney) - the game constantly supports multiple viable approaches. Combine that with the game’s brilliantly designed levels and you have a massive sandbox to play around and engage with for hours. 

I do have mixed feelings about the game’s overall voice acting. The clear high points are the performance of Diana Burnwood (Jane Perry) and Agent 47 (David Bateson). Diana’s delivery is impeccable, channeling an M-esque authority in the vein of Dame Judi Dench, while Agent 47’s constant attempts at deadpan assassin humour provided a delightful contrast. That said, the hundred of generic NPCs scattered throughout the level are a sore point for me. For much of Hitman 1 and 2, background characters default to generic American or British accents regardless of location. You could be in murdering your way through Italy or Bangkok, yet the voices feel oddly out of place - TASTELESS, TRACELESS, and placeholder-esque. Most players probably won’t mind, but I personally felt that for a series so meticulous in its level design, this lack of regional flavour honestly dampened the world-building and immersion. That aside, I’m by no means a  musically-inclined PIANO MAN, but I genuinely did enjoy the atmospheric soundtrack in Hitman WOA. The music is reactive in all the right ways, subtly adapting to your actions during a mission - quiet and restrained when you stalk a target, swelling with tension the moment things begin to unravel. It does an excellent job of reinforcing the game’s mood without ever overpowering the experience. 

Some technical aspects and final notes (please HOLD MY HAIR as I regurgitate them): 
Played exclusively on Steam Deck and while it does work out of the box, it is also quite the energy-intensive (20% battery life for 30 minutes of gameplay). It manages to hold up at a steady 40-50 FPS on medium settings, with dips occurring primarily in crowded levels. You might have trouble reading a fair bit of lore/text (the bios of the various targets you have to eliminate come to mind). Nothing gamebreaking but I had to put on reading glasses to get through a fair bit of text.  Oh and if you’re intending to 100% this, it’s pretty straight-forward. Pretty much every level involves completing it multiple times to achieve mastery level 20. There’s the sniper assassin levels (there’s three of them) and those require a high score that can only be achieved via plenty of practice and unlocking of challenges. Recommended viewing if you’re unsure on how to complete a certain kill method - MrFreeze2244’s youtube channel. Plenty of guides there.   

All in all, Hitman WOA is an exceptional experience that far outweighs its shortcomings. Beneath the confusing purchasing structure and a few immersion hiccups lies one of the most thoughtfully designed stealth game ever made. The meticulously-crafted level and reactive system showcase a dev team that deeply understand player agency and creative freedom. Whether you prefer careful planning or chaotic improvisation, the game constantly adapt to your playstyle. Hitman WOA honestly empowers you to truly feel like a VERSATILE ASSASSIN.

Or in the case of bringing Hitman 1 content into Hitman 2, YOU CAN NO LONGER PORT THE CONTENT FORWARD AT ALL.

I've seen a lot of talk about wanting this to be offered at a discount for people who already own H1 and/or H2.  Personally, I don't really care about that and I think it distracts from the actual scummy practices IOI is engaging in here.  H3 was already $60, so I don't see why it would be discounted now that they are adding H1 and H2 content for free in it.  I view it as buying H3 for $70 and, assuming you are new to the series, getting some content for free.  That isn't an issue.

The problem is if you want to play the H1 content that you already own in H2, they removed the ability to do this if you didn't LAUNCH THE GAME before 1/26/23. The problem is that if want to play the H2 dlc that you already own in H3, you now have to REPURCHASE IT if you didn't LAUNCH THE GAME before 1/26/23. That is absolutely ridiculous.

Even more ridiculous is how they handled this whole situation from a PR standpoint.  First, they make a public statement that with this new WoA product, you would have access to everything and, even for the dlc, you would not have to rebuy anything you already own.  Then, they silently remove functionality to access content you already own not just from the new product, but from the older title, H2, as well!  They completely ignore posts on the forums about it. They ignore support requests about it.  Everyone just assumes it's probably a bug from the store changes.  After all, there are pages on their website and a STICKIED POST ON THE STEAM FORUM explaining the content redemption process for carrying forward content you own.  Well, the pages on their website start silenting being taken down. Still no response to support tickets.  The stickied post is still up claiming that this functionality is still there.  And then a week after the sale ends, haha oops, the  sticky post is taken down and replaced by a new statement explaining that they intentionally removed the ability to carry forward content you already own and you just have to buy it again.  This is ONE PARAGRAPH after a statement ensuring customers that they won't have to rebuy content they already own.  This all feels like they intentionally mislead people.

In summary, I purchased everything except H3 years ago but was taking my time slowing going through the series.  And now, because I hadn't LAUNCHED THE GAME before an arbitrary date, I now either have to rebuy content or CAN'T EVEN ACCESS CONTENT AT ALL.  I shilled this package to some friends that were new to the franchise because I thought this simplification to the store was a good opportunity for new players to get in.  I still think that's the case, but I regret the fact that I probably contributed to IOI making money.  I won't be buying ANYTHING from them again until they show some good will towards those of who spent money on them over the years. I'll play what I already own since I bought it, but honestly this whole thing has really soured the motivation I had to get caught up with the series.

HOWEVER,,, very misleading tactics IOI, please do not misinform users on what they are buying.

Hitman 3 is the final game in the third person stealth assassination series, which continues Agent 47’s story from where the second game ended.

[h1]The Good[/h1]

-	Gameplay is basically the same as the previous two games, so if you enjoyed the series so far you’ll enjoy this third game.

-	New maps are well designed, with plenty of opportunities to distract NPCs and stealth kill your targets, or set up accidental deaths. Berlin changes the format of the mission objectives in an interesting way.

-	Story has a satisfying finish.

-	Framerate is mostly stable on my 5 year old PC (which is slightly more powerful than what is recommended on the store page).

[h1]The Bad[/h1]

-	Will only take around 6 hours to complete if you just play through the story once. (My extra playing time includes replaying all the Hitman 1 & 2 maps again for achievements).

-	The store page is a confusing mess, with several different packages and editions which are clearly designed to trick players into buying content they already own.

-	Even though this is a single player game, it has an always online requirement. If your internet connection (or the game’s servers) drops even for a moment, the game will pause and throw up a distracting error message on screen. This happened to me several times.

-	Elusive target missions are still time limited.

[h1]The Recommendation[/h1]

If you like Hitman you should enjoy playing this series finale, however its massively overpriced so wait for a sale. Check the forums or the guides section for advice on exactly what you need to buy.
